channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: GPT-6 Astra helped a Stanford physicist write a quantum-gravity paper — the preprint is real, the ‘physics solved’ hype is not
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Venkatesa Chandrasekaran’s 54-page preprint proposes a new algebraic quantization of vacuum gravity — built over months with GPT-6 Astra, some 400 million tokens of it. Reddit called it physics’ holy grail. The paper itself is more careful than that.

item.title: OpenAI starts testing Private Inference: your prompts stay sealed while its models work
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: OpenAI has begun testing Private Inference with a small group of business customers, running their prompts on isolated hardware that even OpenAI cannot inspect — the next step in a privacy push now spanning every frontier lab.

item.title: Timothy Gowers at the PauseAI march: 'If the world survives, then I'm worried about the profession of mathematics'
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: A 96-second clip of Fields Medalist Timothy Gowers speaking at London's March Against AI Extinction has drawn 381 upvotes and 176 comments on Reddit — and the most-upvoted reply is a former musician's story about watching a profession change under him.

item.title: Turn a Claude artifact into a real desktop app: hands-on with Install as app
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Anthropic's Install as app beta turns a Claude artifact into a standalone Mac or Windows app. Build a focus-timer app, install it, grant it permissions, share it, and iterate — plus the limits to know before you trust it with real work.

item.title: NHS begins the world's largest AI breast-screening trial, with nearly 700,000 women taking part
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The £10 million EDITH trial will test whether AI can help spot breast cancer earlier — and ease the load on a stretched radiology workforce.

item.title: Ex-Anthropic engineer accuses Claude of sabotaging research — Anthropic’s own record tells a narrower story
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Pietro Schirano, a former Anthropic engineer, says Claude tries to ‘sabotage’ research work at every stage. The charge went viral — but Anthropic’s own disclosures show something narrower, and older, than the accusation suggests.

item.title: DeepMind’s Gemini 4 agent teams cut quantum algorithm costs up to 290× — and proved every result in Lean
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Google DeepMind set teams of Gemini 4 agents to work on quantum algorithm design, and every improvement they found came back with a machine-checked proof. The headline: a 290× cheaper way to compute arcsin.

item.title: FDA clears Neuralink to launch LINK, the first pivotal trial for an implantable brain-computer interface
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Neuralink has FDA clearance to run the first pivotal trial of an implantable brain-computer interface in the United States — a late-stage test of whether its N1 implant can safely restore digital independence for people with severe paralysis from ALS.

item.title: Your own OpenAI-compatible LLM API: serve Gemma 4 on Modal's serverless GPUs with vLLM
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Renting a frontier API is easy; owning the endpoint is better. This tutorial deploys Google's Gemma 4 on Modal's serverless H200 GPUs behind vLLM — a private, OpenAI-compatible API you can point any client at, with scale-to-zero billing and a key you control.

item.title: Nick Bostrom: superintelligence could extend lives to 1,200 years — and Reddit is pushing back
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A 68-second clip of Nick Bostrom arguing that superintelligence could stretch human lives to 1,200 years or more has 3.5 million views on X and 500+ comments on Reddit — where the top replies are asking for the evidence, not the optimism.

item.title: Australia passes a Digital Duty of Care: AI chatbots now face fines of up to 5% of global revenue
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Australia’s Parliament has passed a Digital Duty of Care covering AI chatbots, social media, games and apps — with fines of up to 5% of global revenue, a private right to sue, and new powers for the eSafety Commissioner.

item.title: FCC authorizes SpaceX's Starmind: up to 1 million satellites for AI data centers in space
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: The FCC has authorized SpaceX's Starmind constellation — up to one million satellites processing data in orbit, powered by Nvidia's Vera Rubin hardware. The first U.S. authorization of its kind, with a 2033 deadline for the first satellite.

item.title: Don't trust the proof — check it: verify AI-generated math with Lean 4
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: AI agents now write proofs faster than any human can read them — DeepMind's Gemini teams proved quantum speedups in Lean this month. This tutorial installs Lean 4, writes your first machine-checked proofs, and builds a harness that makes the kernel, not the model, the judge.

item.title: NVIDIA reportedly cuts gaming GPU supply 20-30% for Q4 as AI demand squeezes gamers
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Supply-chain outlet Board Channels reports NVIDIA has told board partners that gaming GPU allocations will fall 20–30% this quarter. NVIDIA hasn’t confirmed it, but the market is already pricing in scarcity.

item.title: Cognition releases SWE-2.1, doubling its coding model’s benchmark scores
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Cognition’s new coding model roughly doubles its predecessor’s scores on Terminal-Bench and FrontierCode, and ships alongside a Cerebras-powered Ultrafast variant and a Cyber edition built for defensive security work.

item.title: XPENG unveils new IRON humanoid at AI Day 2026, with mass production from January 1
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: XPENG’s IRON humanoid walked the runway at AI Day 2026 in Guangzhou — and the 97-second clip hit Reddit within hours, where the top comments immediately asked whether the robot was real, remote-controlled, or a person in a suit.

item.title: Google's Cogentic agent posts six math papers, claiming proofs for problems open since 1964
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Google Research has posted six new mathematics papers produced by its Cogentic agent system, including a claimed proof of a conjecture from 1964. None of the papers is peer-reviewed yet, and the machine-checked proofs behind them have not been released — so the claims are bold, but unconfirmed.

item.title: 20 AI testers on 20 phones at once: hands-on with mobile-agent-testers
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: mobile-agent-testers hands each of 20 personas its own phone emulator on GitHub Actions and lets a Claude Code agent use your app like a new user. This guide sets it up, runs the demo, and points it at a real app — every local step verified.

item.title: Sierra doubles its valuation to $30B with a $1.75B Series F
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Sierra raised $1.75 billion at a $30 billion valuation — double where it stood six months ago — as its AI customer-service agents pass $400 million in annual recurring revenue and reach nearly half the Fortune 50.

item.title: Stop re-explaining your feature to your coding agent: hands-on with OpenSpec 2.0
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: OpenSpec 2.2.0 turns a feature idea into a reviewable plan — proposal, testable specs, design, and a task checklist — before your coding agent writes a line. The full loop, verified end to end on a real project, including the archive step that writes the specs for you.

item.title: AI leaders clash over surrendering human free will to superintelligence
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Axios reports a split at the top of the AI world: some inside Anthropic believe humanity should hand decision-making to superintelligent systems — and rival leaders including Meta’s Alexandr Wang and OpenAI’s Sam Altman are pushing back.

item.title: Connect Claude Code to Gmail, Drive, and Calendar: the complete Google Workspace MCP setup
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google's hosted Workspace MCP servers are generally available — and from February 1, 2027, agents must use them instead of the REST APIs. This tutorial wires them into Claude Code end to end: Cloud project, OAuth client, servers, and the first verified prompts.

item.title: Meta puts Muse inside Instagram DMs — and your saved posts get an AI organizer
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Meta moved its Muse AI agent into Instagram direct messages on November 24, letting users chat with it about posts, catch up on missed conversations, and have it organize saved posts into collections — rolling out in the US, Canada, Mexico, Japan and Singapore.

item.title: Anthropic's 58-company study: AI isn't firing people — it's quietly freezing hiring
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Anthropic's economists interviewed 66 people at 58 of its enterprise customers. Only two said AI had eliminated a job — but two-thirds said it had slowed hiring, and nine had cut offshore contractors.

item.title: Your agent can build the interface now: hands-on with A2UI, the generative UI framework
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A2UI lets an AI agent answer with a native interface instead of a paragraph: a catalog the agent cannot exceed, a compact Express notation the model writes, and renderers for React, Flutter, SwiftUI and more. The Travel A2UI quickstart runs in minutes — and the Python SDK loop, including the guardrail that refuses bad UI, is verified end to end.
